name: Jean Chrétien
summary: A Liberal centrist who as prime minister eliminated the federal deficit through spending cuts, kept universal health care, and defended national unity against Quebec sovereignty with the Clarity Act. He kept Canada out of the 2003 Iraq war for lack of UN approval, brought in firearms registration, banned corporate and union political donations, and moved to legalise same-sex marriage.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Describes Canada's system where basic medical needs are paid for by the state and urges the US to do the same.

public-ownership.rationale: His government privatized Canadian National Railway in 1995 through an initial public offering.

limit-guns.rationale: His government enacted the Firearms Act of 1995 (licensing and registration of firearms).

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In June 2003 he announced the government would accept the court rulings and legislate to legally recognise same-sex marriage, with protection for churches.

abortion-legal.rationale: Calls himself pro-choice, 'for the woman to decide', and says he won't impose his religious limits on others.

free-trade.rationale: Describes himself as a free trader inside his party and says he kept NAFTA with modifications.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: His government committed Canadian forces to the 1999 Kosovo conflict.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Clarity Act says a province's secession needs a constitutional amendment and a clear majority on a clear question, and bars negotiation otherwise; no unilateral right.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Made eliminating the deficit a priority by cutting federal programs, and later surpluses went to tax cuts and debt paydown.

national-self-determination.rationale: Argues that dividing the world along ethnic lines would split many countries, citing Canada's two languages and immigrant mix as the alternative.

force-without-un.rationale: Said Canada always required Security Council approval for taking part in a military campaign and stayed out of Iraq without it; the Kosovo record was not sourced here.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Canada committed to forgive debts owed by heavily indebted poor countries and cancelled aid debts of sub-Saharan African states.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: In 2002 his government pledged $6 billion for Africa over five years and to double international assistance by 2010.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: As justice minister he helped negotiate the patriation of the constitution and the Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: His government passed the 2000 Act implementing the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: His government's Bill C-24 banned corporate and union donations and limited individual contributions.

notes: Researched government, justice, world, liberty and society themes from his own interview, enacted laws and encyclopedia accounts. Most statements stay null for lack of a stated position or sourced record; the memoirs were not available.
